prerequisites: Basic knowledge of fundamental magnitudes: Dimensional, force, flow, pressure, power, electrical, etc.
Very elementary concepts of mechanics, physics, and electricity to understand the principles behind measuring equipment operation.
Basic PC skills (word processor, spreadsheet, file manipulation, etc.)

learning_outcomes.text: Students must have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan in the business field, and other institutions and organizations.
Knowledge of automatic regulation and control techniques and their application to industrial automation.
Basic knowledge of legal and industrial metrology.
Measurement of magnitudes in Mechanical Engineering.
Understand the importance of metrology in industry and manage related standardization regulations.
Be able to select and use appropriate instruments and equipment to measure a specific magnitude.
Handling of industrial part manufacturing plans.
Understand the concepts related to industrial quality and the process of implementing a quality system.

syllabus_topics: Topic 2: Measurement of lengths in two and three dimensions
Dimensional verification. Measurement by comparison. Dimensional control
Quality and quality systems in industry.
Use of the most common length measuring instruments in Mechanical Engineering.
Determination of the elevation of a cam.
Non-contact measurements with optical equipment (TESA visio and optical microscope).
Three-dimensional measurement with mechanical systems. 3D system.
Noise measurement and insulation of ceilings and walls.
Measurement of pressure, humidity, temperature, rotational speeds.
Measurement of layer and wall thicknesses.
teaching_methods: Debate and sharing of topics of interest

assessment_methods.method: Daily tasks (tests, exercises, and problems) with teaching group
Final evaluation of reports and assignments (active participation)
Final evaluation of reports and assignments (report grades)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final exam accounts for 60% of the final grade, and passing the practical sessions and scoring above 4 on the final exam are required to pass the course. For the extraordinary call, course grades can be maintained, or students can opt for the final exam (covering theory and practicals) to count for 80% of the grade, with a practical exam accounting for 20% if practicals were not passed during the course. Passing the practical component (either during the course or in the practical exam) is essential. For the unique final evaluation, a practical exam is 20% and a theoretical-practical written exam is 80%. Misuse of AI for assignments will be considered plagiarism.
